title: Metallurgy Modeling Scientist
description:
Ref 2578337 \| Date: 11 Sept 2026

![Novelis Switzerland SA]( )



Novelis est animé par la volonté de façonner ensemble un monde durable.



En tant que leader mondial de produits et services innovants et le plus grand recycleur d'aluminium au monde d'aluminium, nous travaillons en partenariat avec des clients des secteurs de l'automobile, de l’aéronautique, des canettes et des spécialités pour fournir des solutions qui améliorent les avantages de l'aluminium léger.



Nous disposons d'un réseau coordonné d'opérations de laminage et de recyclage techniquement sophistiquées sur 29 sites dans 9 pays d'Amérique du Nord, d'Amérique du Sud, d'Europe et d'Asie, avec 12,750 employés dans le monde. Le siège se situe à Atlanta, aux États\-Unis.  



Nous comptons parmi nos clients certaines des marques les plus importantes et les plus connues au monde, notamment Coca\-Cola, BMW, Jaguar Land Rover, Airbus, Boeing, Nespresso, Samsung, et d'autres. En outre, Novelis est à la pointe de l'industrie grâce à ses efforts en matière de durabilité et de recyclage.



Participez à notre mission de créer un monde durable et commencez dès que possible à travailler sur notre site de **Sierre**, en Suisse.

**Metallurgy Modeling Scientist (m/f/d)**



Nous recherchons actuellement un ingénieur ou un chercheur hautement motivé et qualifié dans les domaines de l'ingénierie computationnelle, de la science des matériaux, de la métallurgie ou du génie mécanique pour rejoindre notre équipe sur notre site de Sierre, en Suisse.



Le développement et la production futurs d'alliages d'aluminium recyclés de haute qualité nécessitent des processus rapides et adaptatifs qui relient en temps réel le processus de fabrication et la métallurgie, ainsi qu'une prévision précise des performances.







**Vos responsabilités:**



Vous ferez partie de l’équipe chargée de poursuivre le développement de cadres de modélisation avancés en R\&D pouvant être appliqués à différentes activités à l’échelle mondiale. Cela comprend les responsabilités suivantes :



* Développer un cadre d’ingénierie computationnelle intégrée des matériaux (ICME), combinant des modèles basés sur la physique, des approches fondées sur les données et des outils numériques pour des applications à l’échelle industrielle.
* Traduire les connaissances relatives aux alliages d’aluminium, à la métallurgie, au laminage et aux procédés de finition en modèles prédictifs de microstructure et de performance permettant le développement virtuel de procédés et de produits.
* Collaborer avec les sites de production afin de garantir une adoption réussie et la concrétisation de la valeur ajoutée pour l’entreprise.


Merci de postuler avant le 2 octobre 2026\.



\-\-\-\-\-



We are currently seeking a highly motivated and skilled engineer or scientist in the field of Computational Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy, or Mechanical Engineering to join our team at our Sierre location in Switzerland.



The future development and production of high\-quality recycled aluminium alloys require fast and adaptive processes that link process and metallurgy in real time, along with precise performance prediction.







**Your responsabilities:**



You will be part of the team to further develop advanced modelling frameworks in R\&D



that can be applied across different operations globally. This includes the following



responsibilities:



* Develop an Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework, combining physics\-based models, data\-driven approaches, and digital tools for industrial\-scale applications.
* Translate aluminium alloy, metallurgy, rolling and finishing process knowledge into predictive microstructure and performance models that enable virtual process and product development.
* Collaborate with manufacturing sites, ensuring successful adoption and business value realization.


**How to convince us:**



* Master's degree in Materials Science, Metallurgy, Computational Engineering, or a related field; PhD preferred.
* Strong expertise in physical metallurgy, with deep knowledge of texture evolution, recrystallization and precipitation phenomena
* Experience with computational materials engineering approaches and modelling tools such as VPSC, DAMASK, CP\-FEM
* Proficiency in scientific programming and data analysis ( Python, MATLAB or similar).
* Ability to bridge the gap between advanced materials science and industrial application by communicating complex technical concepts clearly across all organizational levels.
* Fluent in English; French is an advantage.
* Demonstrated innovation mindset, curiosity and passion for continuous learning, with a self\-driven, highly autonomous and result\-oriented working style.






Please apply before 2nd October, 2026\.

title: Strategic Sourcing Manager - Raw Material & Surface Treatment
description:
Strategic Sourcing Manager -  Raw Material & Surface Treatment

Purpose of the role:

  *  Developing and executing global sourcing strategies for the assigned direct materials categories:  Raw Material & Surface Treatment
  *  Acting as a business partner to key stakeholders in business (Business Units, Engineering, etc.) and Operations (Product Line Supply Chain, Supplier Quality, Production, Materials Management, etc.)
  *  The global category manager shall sustain the Global Strategic Sourcing Operating Model and provide the supply capability and capacity at best cost to support the company’s future business needs and protection of brand value
  *  Application of aligned sourcing processes, sustainable supplier assessments and development approach, a performing and regulatory compliant supply base footprint shall be established and actively managed, contributing to the enhancement of the supply base performance on Quality, Delivery and Cost (QCD)
  *  Realization of a measurable value >3% in recurring and P&L effective cost reductions per year across the global 3rd party spend in the assigned spend categories accompanied by a leveraged and benchmarked supply base management
  *  Grow and further develop a qualified and performing Best Cost Country Supply Base in line with the companies and operations BCC objectives preferably in Eastern Europe and manage a sustainable spend allocation


Responsibilities:

  *  Management of own material categories (capacity, knowledge management, performance)                
  *  Accountable for contributing to the global Direct Material & Supply Base Performance (QCD)        
  *  Representing own direct material categories within the VAT organization                              
  *  Accountable for the category specific achievement of the objectives of cost optimization, supply base optimization, geographic sourcing footprint and Best Cost Country Sourcing                          
  *  Providing forward-looking guidance on trends, threats and opportunities in own categories (eg. raw materials etc.)                          
  *  Active contribution to the bottom up alignment of the Direct Materials Category Team with the defined / set company objectives                                
  *  Interface to BU / Engineering for Strategic Sourcing activities along with the PDP (IP07) process  
  *  Act as a change agent in regards to main stakeholders
  *  Perform the development of category sourcing strategies applying and complying with defined methods and tools
  *  Active supplier relationship management of the global supply base within its own category perimeter in alignment with the category teams in Switzerland, Malaysia and Romania
  *  Ensure consistent application of all Sourcing Levers
  *  Contribution to main Sourcing KPIs
  *  Assembles and actively leads category specific / cross-functional sourcing board
  *  Actively monitors and performs a supply base risk assessment across its own categories
  *  Participates in and contributes to continuous improvement of direct material practices  


Qualifications:  

  *  5+ years in-depth strategic and operational sourcing experience with a solid working knowledge of global category management
  *  Demonstrated work experience on category specific production techniques and processes
  *  Knowledge about category sourcing markets
  *  Office Software / IT application (esp. Excel, Word, Power Point etc.)
  *  Sourcing in Eastern Europe, Asia and experience in Best Cost Country and spend relocation activities
  *  Working experience within a global complex organization
  *  Experience in the field of machine building, vacuum technology and semiconductors
  *  Cross-function / category team management (min. functional)
  *  Sensible and emphatic communication skills with suppliers, colleagues, internal stakeholders, etc.
  *  Strong analytical skills (risk based) and focus on the essential facts
  *  Able to get results through others, able to multi-task, sense of priority, able to handle stress levels
  *  Good communication skills in German and English (any other language will be a plus)

Head of Investor Relations
==========================

**About Copenhagen Atomics**
----------------------------

At Copenhagen Atomics, we believe that abundant, reliable and affordable energy is fundamental to human progress.

Since 2014, we have been developing a new generation of nuclear energy technology based on thorium molten salt reactors. Our ambition is to industrialize nuclear energy through mass manufacturing, standardized reactor systems and a fundamentally different approach to deployment and economics.

Copenhagen Atomics is approaching 100 employees across Denmark and Switzerland, with a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, technicians and commercial professionals.

As we enter the next phase of our growth, we are looking for an exceptional **Head of Investor Relations** to join our executive team and build the commercial organization that will bring Copenhagen Atomics technology to customers around the world.

**About the role**
------------------

Based in our Zug office, you will take a leading role in Copenhagen Atomics' investor relations and capital\-raising activities.

This is a senior, hands\-on position. You will work closely with our CEO, CFO and existing investor relations colleagues to build relationships with investors and secure the capital required for the company's continued growth.

Approximately 80% of your time will be directly related to investor engagement and capital raising: identifying prospective investors, developing relationships, presenting the Copenhagen Atomics investment case, managing fundraising processes and helping bring investment discussions to a successful close.

You will also help develop our Investor Relations organization in Zug. We expect our Swiss activities to grow significantly over the coming years, with the potential for the Zug organization to reach approximately 30 employees.

For the right candidate, this position offers substantial opportunity to grow in responsibility as the company and our international capital base expand.

**Your key responsibilities**
-----------------------------

**Capital raising**  
Identify, engage and develop relationships with institutional investors, family offices, private investors, venture and growth investors, and other long\-term capital providers.

**Investor relationships**  
Build trusted, long\-term relationships with existing and prospective shareholders and serve as a senior point of contact between investors and Copenhagen Atomics.

**Fundraising execution**  
Work closely with the CEO and management team throughout the fundraising process—from investor identification and initial meetings through due diligence, negotiation and closing.

**Investment narrative**  
Clearly communicate Copenhagen Atomics' technology, commercial strategy, market opportunity and long\-term vision to sophisticated international investors.

**Investor materials and communication**  
Work with management, finance and communications colleagues to develop presentations, financial information, investor updates and other materials supporting our fundraising activities.

**Leadership**  
Help build and develop our Investor Relations team in Zug. Lead by example, support colleagues in making good decisions and create a culture of accountability, integrity and execution.

**International investor network**  
Expand Copenhagen Atomics' relationships with investors in Switzerland, Europe, the American and Asian markets.

**What we are looking for**
---------------------------

You have at least **5 years of relevant experience in capital raising, investor relations, private equity, venture capital, investment banking, corporate finance or a comparable field**.

Ideally, you have personally participated in—and successfully completed—significant equity fundraising transactions for technology, deep\-tech, energy, infrastructure or industrial companies.

You are comfortable speaking directly with sophisticated investors, entrepreneurs, family offices and institutional capital providers.

You combine strong relationship\-building skills with the ability to move discussions toward concrete decisions and transactions.

You have excellent business communication and presentation skills in **English**. Professional proficiency in    is highly desirable.

You are comfortable discussing financial models, company valuations, capitalization structures and investment terms with investors and advisers.

You have high personal integrity and understand that trust and credibility are fundamental to successful investor relationships.

You are comfortable working in a fast\-moving entrepreneurial environment where priorities can change quickly and individual responsibility is high.

You enjoy taking ownership rather than waiting for instructions and are motivated by ambitious, long\-term goals.

Experience with nuclear energy is **not required**. However, intellectual curiosity and the ability to understand and communicate complex technology are essential.

Our culture combines engineering, entrepreneurship and a strong belief in personal responsibility. We value people who challenge assumptions, communicate openly, make decisions and take ownership of results.

**Application**
---------------

If you are interested in joining Copenhagen Atomics, please send us:

* Your CV
* A brief motivation letter explaining why Copenhagen Atomics and this role interest you
* Examples of relevant capital\-raising or investor\-relations experience
* References or recommendations from previous employers or business partners, where available


We are particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate a strong investor network and a track record of building trusted relationships that have resulted in successful capital raises.

**Location:** Zug, Switzerland  
**Function:** Investor Relations / Capital Raising  
**Seniority:** Senior / Leadership  
**Employment:** Full\-time

Legal Advisor \- Commodities Trade Finance \+ Wealth Management
===============================================================



Description de l'entreprise
---------------------------





**Client:**



Our client is an established Swiss financial institution with an international client base and activities spanning Commodity Trade Finance, Wealth Management and Treasury. The Bank is looking for a pragmatic, commercially\-minded Legal Advisor to join its Legal \& Compliance function and provide hands\-on legal support across the business. A bank that Finders know well, thus able to explain the culture and working environment to any potentially, suitable applicant.



Description du poste
--------------------





**Position:**



Reporting to the Head of Legal \& Compliance, you will provide day\-to\-day legal advice across the Bank, helping the business navigate legal and regulatory matters while taking a practical and solutions\-focused approach. You will work closely with colleagues across the business, particularly Commodity Trade Finance, Wealth Management, Financial Institutions and Compliance, and will also liaise with clients, external counsel and Swiss authorities where required.



**Key Responsibilities:**



* Provide legal advice and practical guidance to the Bank's various departments on Swiss and international legal matters.
* Draft, review and negotiate banking agreements, security documentation and other legal documents, particularly in relation to Commodity Trade Finance and Wealth Management.
* Support the Bank on legal matters involving clients, counterparties, authorities, courts and bankruptcy offices.
* Advise on client succession and estate\-related matters.
* Review internal policies, directives and standard documentation and ensure they remain aligned with applicable legislation.
* Monitor developments in Swiss banking legislation and regulation and advise the Head of Legal \& Compliance on their impact on the Bank.
* Work with Compliance on cross\-functional legal and regulatory matters.
* Coordinate external lawyers on specialist advice, disputes and litigation where required.
* Conduct legal research and prepare opinions, reports and other legal documentation.
* Provide legal and regulatory training to colleagues where appropriate.
* Act as a deputy to the Head of Legal \& Compliance on legal matters when required.


**Why Apply?**



A good opportunity for a Swiss\-qualified lawyer looking for a varied in\-house position within a specialist banking environment, rather than a narrowly defined legal role. You will have genuine exposure to the business, including Commodity Trade Finance, Wealth Management and Financial Institutions, within an international and multicultural organisation. The role offers considerable variety and the opportunity to take ownership of matters while working closely with experienced colleagues and senior stakeholders.



Profil recherché
-----------------





**Profile:**



* Swiss\-qualified lawyer, ideally with Brevet d'avocat
* Proven experience in Swiss banking law
* Commodity Trade Finance experience is essential
* understanding of Swiss banking regulations and related regulatory/compliance matters
* Strong legal drafting, research and analytical skills
* Experience reviewing and negotiating commercial and banking documentation
* Pragmatic, commercially\-minded approach with sound judgement
* Well organised and able to manage multiple matters and deadlines
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills

title: Senior Lead, Indirect Procurement
description:
The Royal Caribbean Group’s Supply Chain Team has an exciting career opportunity for a full time Senior Lead, Indirect Procurement reporting to the Manager, Indirect Procurement.  
This position is onsite and based in Basel Switzerland. 

Summary

Celebrity River is a new and highly strategic growth platform within Celebrity Cruises, created to redefine the premium river cruise experience through innovation, design excellence and the unparalleled service synonymous with the Celebrity brand. As the business stands up its European footprint, Celebrity River requires a Basel-based Senior Lead, Indirect Procurement to serve as the on-the-ground extension of the Miami Procurement department across Europe.
Based in Basel, Switzerland and working in close partnership with the Miami headquarters, this leader will be the primary facilitator for identifying, screening, contracting, and onboarding the suppliers and vendors that will support Celebrity River’s European operations. The role sits at the intersection of Product Development, Basel Operations & Execution, Procurement, and Legal. The individual will act as a cultural and operational mediator between US and European business practices, ensuring that vendor selection and onboarding processes designed in Miami translate effectively to the realities of the European – and specifically the river cruising – supplier landscape.

The ideal candidate combines a purchasing/procurement background with strong negotiating capability, deep familiarity with European geography and the waterways of Europe, and working knowledge of the river cruising industry and its stakeholder landscape. This is a Senior Lead-level position embedded in the Basel office infrastructure and working closely with European colleagues day to day, while reporting functionally into the Miami Procurement organization – offering meaningful career growth as Celebrity River scales.
This role requires 50% international travel and time onboard vessels.

Key Responsibilities

Vendor and Supplier Onboarding
Facilitate the end-to-end onboarding and contracting of European suppliers and vendors for Celebrity River, from initial identification through final contract execution including procure to pay management.
Prepare and manage vendor screening, information gathering, and the selection process for prospective suppliers as well as onboarding process in our systems.
Build and maintain stakeholder mapping, evaluation criteria sets, and vendor profiling to support consistent, well-documented selection decisions.
Design and continuously refine the onboarding process so it can scale efficiently as the vendor base grows tracking cycle times.
Support end-to-end source-to-pay execution, including supplier onboarding, system setup, requisition and purchase order coordination, invoice/payment issue escalation, and adherence to procurement system requirement

Cross-Cultural and Cross-Functional Liaison

Coordinate contract lifecycle activities, including intake, routing, approval tracking, amendments, renewals, expiration monitoring, and documentation in accordance with company requirements.

Procurement, Negotiation and Supply Chain
Apply strong negotiating capabilities to secure favorable commercial terms, pricing, and contractual conditions, under a total cost of ownership perspective, with European suppliers and vendors.
Develop and execute sourcing strategies that support operational readiness, scalability, service excellence, and cost efficiency across the European business.
Support the handling of supply chain activities relevant to Celebrity River’s European vendor network, from sourcing through delivery readiness.
Develop and maintain strategic supplier relationships, ensuring long-term alignment with operational, service quality, performance metrics and commercial objectives.
Monitor vendor compliance with contractual obligations, service standards, and agreed performance indicators.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives with suppliers to enhance quality, efficiency, innovation, performance and value.
Establish governance processes, risk mitigation strategies, and ensures compliance across all procurement activities.
Identify and mitigate risks related to supply chain disruptions, quality issues, and contractual obligations in a long-term basis.
Promote the adoption of digital tools, data analytics and implements opportunities for process automation and digital tools to improve procurement efficiency.
Build and maintain a value creation pipeline through savings, cost avoidance, improved commercial terms, demand management, process efficiencies, and supplier innovation; provide recurring reporting to Procurement leadership.
Ensure procurement activity complies with company policies, approval authorities, supplier due diligence requirements, competitive bid expectations, documentation standards, and ethical sourcing practices.

European and River Cruising Market Expertise
Leverage a strong European geography background and knowledge of the waterways of Europe / river cruising to inform vendor sourcing and site-specific supplier decisions.
Maintain current knowledge of the European river cruising landscape and its key stakeholders, competitors, and suppliers to inform sourcing strategy.
Provide market intelligence and on-the-ground perspective to Miami-based Procurement leadership on European supplier trends, norms, and best practices.
Conduct benchmarking and market analysis to identify emerging suppliers, industry trends, cost drivers, and procurement best practices across the European river cruise sector.
Maintain awareness of economic, geopolitical, and supply chain developments that may impact supplier availability, pricing, or operational continuity.

Contribute to a supportive office culture, working collaboratively with European colleagues while also functioning independently on day-to-day procurement and onboarding activity.
Model strong team-player behavior while demonstrating the independence needed to manage vendor relationships and timelines with minimal direct oversight.

Strong analytical and financial acumen with the ability to evaluate commercial proposals and supplier business cases.
Experience with procurement systems, supplier onboarding platforms, contract management tools, and ERP systems (S2P Suites like Oracle, SAP, Coupa).
Advanced Microsoft office and reporting skills.
Knowledge of European procurement regulations and vendor due diligence practices preferred.
Comfortable working remotely for a Miami-based department while embedded in a European office environment.
Proficiency in English and German.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Procurement, Finance, Engineering or a related field required.
Professional certification in procurement or supply chain management a plus.
Strong team player who also works well independently, managing vendor pipelines and deadlines with limited oversight.
Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to manage stakeholder mapping, criteria sets, and vendor profiling processes rigorously.

Educational activities assistant (4 months replacement sick leave: 70\-100%)
============================================================================











We are currently seeking an **Educational activities assistant** for a **4\-month temporary position (70–100%)** to support the coordination and delivery of ERS educational assessment activities, with a particular focus on the Adult and Paediatric HERMES examinations. The successful candidate will provide operational and administrative support, coordinate examination\-related activities, and work closely with expert committees, faculty members and international partners. The role requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail, a proactive approach and the ability to manage multiple tasks in a collaborative, international environment.







Educational activities assistant (4 months replacement sick leave: 70\-100%)
============================================================================



**Role purpose**
----------------



The Educational Activities Assistant supports the delivery of ERS assessment activities, with a particular focus on the HERMES examinations for adult and paediatric. Working closely within the education team and the Assessment Director, Examination Committees, MCQ authors, national societies and internal stakeholders, the role ensures high\-quality assessment processes, supports the international development of HERMES examinations and contributes to the continuous evolution of ERS educational standards.







**Key contribution areas**
--------------------------



### **1\. Governance \& operational coordination**



Coordinate the operational planning and governance of ERS assessment activities by ensuring effective committees and MCQ authors support, examination delivery and continuous process improvement.



**Key responsibilities**



* Assist in the operational planning and delivery of the Adult and Paediatric HERMES examinations.  
* Support Examination Committees activities, meetings, documentation and follow\-up actions.  
* Monitor project plans, budgets, milestones and examination timelines to ensure timely delivery.  
* Prepare reports, presentations, statistics and operational documentation supporting committee activities and decision\-making.  
* Identify opportunities to improve operational processes and examination delivery.  


### **2\. Learning pathways, assessments, accreditation \& certification**



Ensure the quality, relevance and continuous development of ERS assessment activities by coordinating examination processes, supporting assessment design and promoting recognised educational standards.



**Key responsibilities**



* Assist in the development and delivery of the Adult and Paediatric HERMES examinations and other assigned assessment programmes.  
* Support the continuous review and maintenance of examination blueprints, syllabi, question banks and assessment documentation.  
* Coordinate MCQ author recruitment, onboarding, training and performance evaluation.  
* Contribute to the development of innovative assessment approaches, digital examination solutions and AI\-supported translation/ initiatives where appropriate.  


### **3\. Global engagement, partnerships \& capacity building**



Strengthen the international recognition and reach of ERS assessment programmes by developing partnerships, supporting national societies and promoting capacity building among assessment contributors.



**Key responsibilities**



* Coordinate translation initiatives to broaden access to ERS examinations and support multilingual delivery where appropriate.  
* Maintain effective internal and external relationships with partners, providers and officers.  
* Benchmark assessment practices and contribute to the continuous evolution of ERS examination programmes.  


### **4\. Collaboration \& cross\-functional Contribution**



Contribute to a collaborative and high\-performing working environment by fostering teamwork, knowledge sharing and effective cross\-functional collaboration across ERS.



**Key responsibilities**



* Build effective working relationships across ERS departments and with external partners.  
* Acquire knowledge and contribute to cross\-functional initiatives supporting organisational priorities.  
* Promote collaborative ways of working and continuous improvement across projects and partnerships.  
* On an ad hoc basis, contribute to projects and initiatives beyond the role’s defined responsibilities, in support of broader organisational needs.  


Education \& professional background
------------------------------------



* Bachelor’s or master’s degree in education, health sciences, business administration, project management or a related discipline.  
* Experience coordinating educational assessments, certification programmes or complex educational projects.  
* Experience working with expert committees, examination boards or professional associations.  
* Experience in an international scientific, medical, educational or not\-for\-profit environment is an advantage.  


Your profile
------------





*  **A strong team player** with excellent interpersonal and communication skills  
* High attention to detail and a solution\-oriented mindset  
* Excellent command of **English**  
* Strong multitasking, prioritisation, proactiveness and time management skills  
* Proficient in MS Office  
* Swiss or Swiss work permit holder  
* Available immediately or at short notice

-------------------



If you are interested in this position and see yourself contributing to our mission, please submit your full application (cover letter and CV).

description:
Job Description:
The Risk Officer, Base Metals is a member of the Risk team, reporting to the EMEA Risk Team Lead. He/She is responsible for leading research and analysis, delivering reports, and high-quality digital tools to improve decision making and risk management of base metals desk.

Main Responsibilities
Daily reporting of P&L, exposures, VaR and explanation thereof.
Manage daily checks on, trade capture, trade integrity and completeness between desks and trading system.
Monitor forward curves and volatilities for accuracy and consistency.
Provide analytical support to the traders on base metals.
Check and assist in capturing and evaluating the risk of complex products.
Apply risk-reserving methodology to trading P&L.
Responsible for monthly translation into accounting of trading results.
Month end and year end reconciliations with finance and external auditors as required.
Improve existing and develop new daily procedures for management reporting, trade completeness, market data and other such processes as required.
Liaise closely with IT, Operations, Credit Risk, Finance, and Front Office.
Prepare various reports and analysis for publishing internally and to the Management Board as the case may be.

Base metals MO should have below additional specific knowledge:
For physical:
London Metals Exchange (LME) pricing mechanics: LME 3M, LME Cash, LME 3rd Wed (monthly settlement) and daily rings (for diff metals), and potentially corresponding knowledge of exchange CME and SHFE.
MtM valuations according to time spreads and arbitrages locked (i.e. LME vs SHFE)
MtM valuations of various grades of diff metals, quantify and sense check the discounts or premiums.
Cost accruals reconciliation according to the delivery locations, spreads locked and freight market.
Term contracts and allocation with spot deals
Exchange delivery and warrant trading.
Solid understanding of the “repos” physical deals (“repurchase deals”) i.e in substance a loan using base metals as collateral or genuine buy/sell trades.

For paper:
Familiar with various granularity and expiry of the liquid paper contracts (LME 3M, Cash, daily and monthly; SHFE monthly; CME monthly)
FX hedging if material quantity done on SHFE
Sense check liquidity risk of long dated contracts (i.e. 1 year forward contract)

Profile
University degree, preferably in Computing, Mathematics, Engineering, Economics or Finance.
Mastery of analytics tools and technologies.
Minimum 3 years in a similar role in the commodity trading business, preferably within a major trading house, an oil major, an investment bank or a hedge fund.
Very good knowledge of Excel and VBA.
Good knowledge of Access and SQL Server
Fluent in English, both written and spoken, French is a plus.
Curious and Proactive
Eager to learn and ability to work with limited supervision.·       Rigorous and meticulous
Strong communication skills
Highly numerate
Strong team spirit

title: Head of Years (Up to Year 4)
description:
JOB PURPOSE
Aiglon College is an international boarding school based in the Swiss Alps with a worldwide reputation for providing a challenging and transformational holistic education in an inspiring setting within a safe, caring and supportive framework. The School is CIS accredited, and caters for 500 students aged 5-18 representing 65 nations. In their final years students prepare for Cambridge IGCSEs and the IB Diploma Programme but our distinct learning philosophy begins to become embedded from our youngest students. The Junior school is a connected part of the whole school but is also a distinct section separate from the Senior School with a dedicated focus on students up to Year 8.

The school wishes to appoint, for August 2027 (possibly January or April 2027 for the right candidate), an innovative, caring, and dynamic Head of Years (Up to Year 4) who will provide operational leadership, and support strategic development, for the lower junior phase up to Year 4, line manage class teachers and teaching assistants up to Year 4, and work in close partnership with the Director of Junior School and Head of Junior Curriculum and Academics.

The ideal candidate for this position would be an experienced primary/early years specialist with leadership experience, ideally in an international setting, who has expertise in early childhood education, literacy and numeracy foundations, and outdoor/experiential learning. Knowledge of inquiry based learning, project based learning, or biophilic education would be preferable.

This position involves a teaching component and presents a unique opportunity to lead and nurture our youngest learners in a world-class alpine environment.

KEY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

To put the students first.
To lead the day-to-day operational and educational provision for students up to Year 4, working in close partnership with and under the strategic oversight of the Head of Junior Curriculum and Academics.
To participate actively in Junior School Leadership Team meetings and contribute to strategic planning for the lower primary phase.
Direct line management of classroom teachers and teaching assistants across years up to Year 4, fostering a collaborative, supportive, and high-performing staff team.
Direct operational delivery and coordination of the Mountain School programme up to Year 4, working closely with the Head of Junior Expeditions and the Head of Junior Curriculum and Academics.
To be the primary point of contact for day-to-day academic, pastoral, and operational matters for families and day students up to Year 4.
To uphold the ethos and values of the school and to be a role model for staff and students.
Become involved in discipline and pastoral matters up to Year 4, ensuring student behavior aligns with school expectations.
To ensure smooth transition and induction for children entering Year 1 and progressing through to Year 4, preparing them seamlessly for upper junior years (Years 5-6).
To ensure the Guiding Principles are embedded throughout the daily routine and learning environment of students up to Year 4.
To participate in staff recruitment for lower junior phase positions as required by the Director of Junior School and Head of Junior Curriculum and Academics.
To carry out tasks as delegated by the Director of Junior School and Head of Junior Curriculum and Academics.
To be a classroom teacher with a reduced teaching load (approx 20% reduction).
To embrace innovative forms of assessment, play-based learning, and holistic reporting for young learners.

Responsibility for the Wellbeing and Safeguarding of Students

To oversee the daily pastoral care, wellbeing, and progress tracking of all students up to Year 4.
To appreciate the key role of safeguarding in managing student interventions and work closely with the Junior School DSL, Director of Junior School, and wellbeing team.
To work with the Director of Junior School, Head of Junior Curriculum and Academics and Junior School DSL in the implementation of policies and statements of good practice for safeguarding, wellbeing, and healthcare in lower primary.
To implement a nurturing and sequential Wellbeing programme across years up to Year 4 aligned with the Spirit Curriculum.
To promote Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion formally within the Spirit Curriculum to build a kind, positive, and inclusive culture among young learners.
To liaise with the Junior Activities Coordinator and House teams to ensure appropriate co-curricular activities, sports, and outdoor experiences for students up to Year 4.

Academic Responsibilities

To lead the daily implementation and delivery of the lower junior curriculum (up to Year 4), including the 'Wonder' projects and early literacy/numeracy frameworks.
To work closely with the Head of Junior Expeditions to plan and deliver the experiential Mountain School curriculum for students up to Year 4.
To champion sustainability, outdoor exploration, and biophilic education within the classroom and Mountain School activities.
To ensure Aiglon's Guiding Principles for learning are embedded in all teaching and learning activities for students up to Year 4.
To assist in monitoring student progress, organising learning interventions, and supporting personalised learning in coordination with the Head of Learning Support and Head of EAL.
To support the Head of Junior Curriculum and Academics in teacher professional reviews and development for staff who teach up to Year 4.
To assist in overseeing internal assessments, reporting structures, and parent-teacher communication up to Year 4.
To promote and ensure effective and safe usage of school educational technology (such as Google Apps for Education and age-appropriate devices).
To participate in staff development days and continuous professional learning for the lower primary phase.
To monitor and enhance standards of teaching, learning, and classroom environment up to Year 4.
Undertake any other task which may be reasonably required by the Director of the Junior School or Head of Junior Curriculum and Academics.
Understand and implement all school policies and procedures, particularly those relating to safeguarding children and young people.
Understand the School’s Guiding Principles and uphold the ethos of the School at all times.
Embrace artificial intelligence and other related educational innovations to enhance early learning experiences.

This job outline only contains the main accountabilities relating to the post of Head of Years (Up to Year 4) and does not describe in detail all of the duties required to carry them out. The Head of Years (Up to Year 4) may be required to undertake other duties and responsibilities that are commensurate with the nature and level of the post.

Chief of Staff (a) (80\-100%)
=============================




**Technology \& Leadership – dafür steht Consult \& Pepper. Als spezialisierte Personalberatung besetzen wir seit über 25 Jahren anspruchsvolle Fach\- und Führungspositionen. Dabei arbeiten wir branchenagnostisch mit Start\-Ups, KMUs und internationalen Grosskonzernen zusammen.**

**Unsere Unternehmenskultur ist geprägt von einem familiären Miteinander, offener und manchmal etwas sehr direkter Kommunikation sowie einem starken Teamgeist. Kollegiale Unterstützung, kurze Entscheidungswege und gemeinsame Events sorgen dafür, dass Arbeit bei uns nicht nur erfolgreich, sondern auch menschlich ist.**

**Zur Unterstützung unserer beiden Co\-CEOs suchen wir ein neugieriges, lernfähiges und umsetzungsstarkes Organisationstalent mit hoher Technologieaffinität als « Chief of Staff».**




**Deine Herausforderung**

Du stehst kurz vor deinem Studienabschluss oder hast diesen gerade hinter dir – und suchst keinen klassischen Einstiegsjob? Du möchtest nicht in einem Traineeprogramm eine Station von vielen durchlaufen, sondern direkt erleben, wie ein Unternehmen geführt wird?  
In dieser vielseitigen Stabsrolle erhältst du Einblick in nahezu alle Bereiche eines KMUs, unterstützt die Geschäftsleitung im operativen Tagesgeschäft und übernimmst zunehmend eigene Projekte und Verantwortungsbereiche.

Deine Aufgabenschwerpunkte sehen wie folgt aus – wobei sich deine im Laufe der Zeit verändern und weiterentwickeln wird.

* **Management Support \& Business Operations (\~40%)**
    + Du unterstützt unsere beiden Co\-CEOs im operativen Tagesgeschäft und hältst ihnen bei administrativen und organisatorischen Aufgaben den Rücken frei
    + Du bereitest Präsentationen, Auswertungen, Controllings und Entscheidungsgrundlagen auf
    + Du koordinierst zentrale interne Abläufe und entwickelst bestehende Instrumente und Prozesse weiter
    + Du bist Anlaufstelle für unsere Mitarbeitenden bei organisatorischen und administrativen Fragestellungen
* **Provider Management \& Infrastruktur (\~15%)**
    + Du koordinierst schrittweise unsere externen Partner und Dienstleister, insbesondere in den Bereichen IT, LinkedIn und Jobplattformen
    + Du verwaltest zentrale Firmenaccounts, Lizenzen und Verträge und behältst Kosten, Laufzeiten und Leistungen im Blick
    + Du stellst gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern sicher, dass unsere Mitarbeitenden über eine funktionierende und zeitgemässe Arbeitsumgebung verfügen
* **Marketing \& Kommunikation (\~20%)**
    + Du gestaltest unseren Unternehmensauftritt auf LinkedIn sowie weitere zentrale Kommunikationskanäle mit
    + Du verantwortest unser Newslettering und unterstützt bei der Weiterentwicklung unserer Website
    + Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit dem Team Marketing\- und Kundenaktivitäten
* **Digitalisierung, AI \& Projekte (\~25%)**
    + Du treibst Projekte in den Bereichen AI, Digitalisierung und Business Development voran
    + Du beobachtest technologische Entwicklungen und prüfst, wie neue Tools und AI\-Anwendungen bei C\&P sinnvoll eingesetzt werden können
    + Du unterstützt die Co\-CEOs bei konzeptionellen und strategischen Projekten und bringst diese in die Umsetzung



**Deine Qualitäten und Begabungen**

Senior Associate – Treasury Strategy \& Technology
====================================================







100%



**Your Impact**



**\- Strategic Advisory at the Highest Level:** You will advise international corporations on complex treasury, financial risk management, and cash management challenges, with a specific focus on treasury technology, systems architecture, and digital transformation.  
**\- Transformational Impact:** You will help drive large\-scale, multi\-stakeholder transformation initiatives at global companies \- reshaping how treasury functions operate, create value, and leverage technology.  
**\- AI \& Innovation Leadership:** You will be at the forefront of applying artificial intelligence and machine learning to treasury and financial processes \- from cash flow forecasting and liquidity optimization to fraud detection, risk modeling, and intelligent automation.  
**\- Thought Leadership:** You will provide thought leadership and practical, actionable advice on treasury strategy, financial risk management, regulatory compliance, and the evolving role of technology in finance.  
**\- Efficiency \& Value Creation:** You will improve the added value, operational efficiency, internal controls, and regulatory compliance of clients' treasury functions and their supporting technology ecosystems.  
**\- Collaborative Excellence:** You will collaborate with a diverse, global network of highly talented experts across strategy, technology, risk, and finance \- sharing knowledge and building innovative solutions together.  
**\- Diverse, International Environment:** You will work across multiple industries, service areas, and geographies in a dynamic and stimulating professional setting.



**Your Skill Set**



**Experience \& Qualifications**



* 3 \- 6 years of relevant professional experience in treasury consulting, treasury technology, financial risk management, or within a corporate treasury function with a strong systems and technology focus.
* University degree (Master's preferred) in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Financial Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
* Professional certification such as CFA, FRM, CTP, or equivalent qualification, demonstrating deep expertise in financial analysis, accounting, and financial risk management.
**Technical \& Domain Expertise** * Deep financial analysis and risk management skills, including a strong understanding of financial instruments, hedge accounting, valuation methodologies, interest rate and FX risk, and treasury\-related accounting standards (IFRS 9, etc.).
* In\-depth, hands\-on knowledge of at least one leading Treasury Management System (TMS) such as FIS (Quantum/Integrity), Kyriba, Coupa Treasury, ION (IT2/Wallstreet Suite), SAP Treasury, or similar \- including implementation, configuration, and optimization experience.
* Familiarity with treasury processes and operations, including cash and liquidity management, bank relationship management, payments and bank connectivity (SWIFT, host\-to\-host), debt and investment management, and intercompany financing.
* Deep knowledge of the application of AI and machine learning to financial processes, including predictive analytics for cash forecasting, anomaly detection, natural language processing for financial data, robotic process automation (RPA), and the integration of intelligent solutions into treasury workflows.
* Understanding of the broader treasury technology ecosystem, including ERP integration, data architecture, API connectivity, cloud\-based solutions, and emerging fintech platforms.
**Personal \& Professional Attributes** * Exceptional analytical and problem\-solving capabilities, with the ability to synthesize complex financial, operational, and technical information into clear, compelling recommendations.
* Strong presentation and communication skills, with confidence and credibility when interacting with senior client stakeholders, including C\-suite executives and treasury leadership.
* An advisory and team\-oriented mindset \- you take ownership of workstreams, mentor junior team members, foster innovative thinking, and contribute to a culture of excellence.
* Comfort working in a dynamic, fast\-paced environment, both independently and as part of cross\-functional, international teams.
* Fluent English (written and spoken) is required; , French, or any additional language is a strong plus.
* A commitment to expanding our global business network and leveraging your personal and professional relationships to create opportunities and deepen client trust.


**Your Contact**



Jacsman



**About PwC**

title: Lead Electrical Engineer (100%)
description:
Get to know Climeworks
Climeworks is a leading high-quality carbon removal provider, combining decades of expertise in Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology with a holistic approach to carbon removal solutions.

Climeworks advises companies on their carbon removal strategies and provides tailored portfolios of nature-based and engineered approaches, offering end-to-end services to help achieve net-zero goals. The company runs the world's first two DAC plants in Iceland, demonstrating its core commitment to high-quality carbon removal that is backed by over 15 years of pioneering research, development, and deployment.

By advancing the most reliable solutions in the market, Climeworks accelerates the global transition to net zero, unlocking economic value for businesses, governments, and society.

We foster a dynamic environment and are building a global purpose driven team. We are looking for disruptive thinkers, passionate achievers and inspiring leaders that are ready to take on the world’s greatest challenge.

Will you join us?

Your mission
Job description
Technical Direction: You define and maintain the technical direction for the Electrical Department.  You lead the development of fit-for-purpose EIC specifications, design philosophies, and basis of design for execution Globally. You ensure owner requirements are clearly defined, documented, and communicated to contractors, and validate design assumptions against operability and safety, and ensure compliance with local and regional codes and regulations.

Contractor management: You review and approve contractor submissions for electrical systems and power distribution, enforce owner requirements, provide technical clarifications, and ensure adherence to schedule, quality, safety, and operability. You set clear expectations for execution methods, field quality controls, and turnover documentation needed for safe operation and maintenance.

System Reliability & Innovation: You lead initiatives to improve reliability and performance of Electrical systems, troubleshoot issues, and implement preventive measures. You evaluate and introduce emerging technologies such as energy efficiency solutions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: You act as the primary Electrical interface with process, instrumentation and controls, mechanical, and project management teams to ensure integrated designs. You identify and mitigate Electrical risks during design and operation phases and support project teams with scope, cost, and schedule estimates.

Team Leadership & Continuous Improvement: You supervise and coach junior team members, provide guidance on technical challenges, and drive lessons-learned sessions to maintain a strong knowledge base and promote continuous improvement.  You maintain thorough records of technical decisions, design bases, vendor information, and lessons learned for future operational use.

Cold-Weather and Constructability: As our next DAC plant could be in a cold or hot weather environment, you incorporate climate conditions into the Electrical design and execution planning (extreme heat, freeze protection, winterization, insulation/heat tracing philosophy, cold start/commissioning constraints). You ensure the design is constructable and able to operate and be maintained through cold or hot conditions, including consideration of temporary works, for instance winter work sequencing, and interface constraints with cold-weather activities.

Your story
Requirements
Professional Experience: You have a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or equivalent and have at least 10 years of experience in process plants various climates as an Electrical Engineer.  You have experience leading teams.

Project Experience: You have hands-on involvement in at least one full-cycle project in the mining, water treatment, oil and gas or other comparable industries, covering all phases from FEED and detailed design to construction, commissioning and start-up; preferably in remote/seasonally constrained execution environments.  You have expertise in low and medium voltage electrical systems, industrial instrumentation, and control systems.

Cold-Weather Industrial Plant Experience: You have hands-on experience working with industrial plants in cold-weather environments (e.g. Canada, Nordic countries, or similar climates) and understand the operational, maintenance, and safety challenges associated with extreme weather conditions.

Communication & Collaboration: You demonstrate excellent written and verbal communication skills and can liaise with diverse stakeholders, including third-party vendors in IP-sensitive collaborations.

Working Style: You are precise, adaptable, and reliable, with a proactive and solution-oriented approach. You are comfortable driving decisions and owning them in the office and under field constraints, including winter productivity and schedule risk.  You are highly organized, able to plan and prioritize work for yourself and others, and comfortable working in fast-paced environments.

Language Skills and Travel: You are fluent in English and ready to travel up to 40% of your time (including extended site presence during peak design, engineering, construction and commissioning periods).

Our promise: At Climeworks, you are accepted for who you are, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued. We encourage all qualified applicants to apply – regardless of background, identity, or experience. Studies show that women and individuals from minority backgrounds often only apply for jobs when they meet 100% of the listed criteria. If this sounds like you, don’t hold back. If you think you’d make a great fit for this role, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t check every single box. Let’s tackle one of humankind’s greatest challenges together.

What we offer:

Time Off: Enjoy 25 paid vacation days every year, plus public holidays.

Flexibility: Work how it suits you best. We offer a hybrid work setup and up to 4 weeks of remote work annually within any EU country.

Ownership: Fair base pay paired with an equity package – because your contributions matter.

Family Support: Inclusive parental leave.

Continuous Learning: Dedicated budget to invest in your professional growth.

Referral Rewards: Help us grow our team and earn bonuses for your successful referrals.

Salary: At Climeworks, salary ranges are assigned to a job based on the level of seniority and the location specific market median of similar jobs according to external benchmark surveys. Individual compensation depends on your skills, experience, and the value you bring to the team.

Formalities:

This position is based in Opfikon, Zurich, and we ask that you work onsite at least three days per week.

We do not accept candidate profiles through recruitment agencies.

Deputy School Director (Academic)
=================================







**Aiglon College** seeks to appoint a suitably qualified











Deputy School Director (Academic)
=================================



to join the school from: **23\.08\.2027**



**Your profile**



The role and candidate profile for this role is detailed in the attached job description and person specification.



Successful Aiglon staff are enthusiastic, experienced, committed, reflective, dynamic and willing to try new ideas. If you share these values and have an appetite for challenge and an ambition to make a positive impact on our world, we welcome your application.



**About us**



Located in Chesières (Vaud, Switzerland), Aiglon College is a not\-for\-profit, international boarding school offering a distinctive, world\-class education in a stunning alpine setting.



The school was founded on a distinctive ethos: the balanced development of mind, body and spirit. This philosophy underpins everything we do at Aiglon, both inside and outside the classroom.



There are over 480 students, representing more than 70 nationalities, following the International GCSE (IGCSE) and International Baccalaureate Diploma (IB Diploma) programmes.



**What we offer**



Aiglon is dedicated to the well\-being and professional development of all staff, within a vibrant, friendly, and modern workplace. Beyond competitive salaries and comprehensive social security benefits, we provide free accident and loss of salary insurances, generous pension and leave entitlements, as well as a range of special perks and advantages.



**How to apply**



Deadline for applications: **23\.10\.2026**



Early applications are encouraged. We reserve the right to appoint before the application deadline should we find the right candidate. Please apply through our School platform (eteach) following the instructions; applications sent by standard email will not be considered.



**Aiglon is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.**



**Applicants will therefore need to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post.**



You can find information on how the School processes your personal data within the School’s .



**JOB PURPOSE**



The role of Deputy School Director is a key management and leadership position in the school, and they are a pivotal member of both the School Council (the leadership team) overseeing many aspects of the operational management and leadership of the School. The role is primarily concerned with the school's academic leadership, with the other Deputy School Directors leading and managing school safeguarding, wellbeing, character education and boarding functions. Additionally, the Deputy School Director is an integral part of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT), working alongside the School Director, CFO/COO, and other Deputy School Directors. Aiglon, distinguished by its philosophy and ethos, prioritises the holistic development of every child. As a school committed to character development and holistic education, we prioritise the student experience and ensure their wellbeing and safety, which are fundamental to their journey at Aiglon.



**OBJECTIVES**



*      To deputise for the School Director as and when required.

  

*      To manage all academic aspects of the school.

  

*      The following list should not be considered definitive but act as a guide to those areas for which the Deputy School Director will be responsible.

  



**KEY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**



**MEMBERSHIP OF THE SCHOOL LEADERSHIP TEAM**



1.      To be a member of the School Council and the ELT.

  

2.      To uphold the ethos and values of the school and to be a role model for staff and students.

  

3.      To ensure student needs and interests are placed at the forefront of all decisions made at the school.

  

4.      To be fully involved in the whole\-school strategic planning and implementing and developing the school’s vision of education.

  

5.      To be the representative and advocate for all direct reports.

  

6.      To work with all members of the School Council to ensure that students’ education is appropriate, broad, balanced and effective across all aspects of school life and that the well\-being and safeguarding of students are prioritised.

  

7.      Understand and implement all school policies and procedures, particularly those relating to safeguarding children and young people.

  

8.      Understand the School’s Guiding Principles and uphold the ethos of the School at all times.

  



**MANAGEMENT AND LEADERSHIP OF ACADEMIC ASPECTS OF THE SCHOOL, INCLUDING LEARNING, TEACHING, AND ASSESSMENT**



1.      To monitor and evaluate the quality of teaching and learning in the school and to be proactive in devising and implementing strategies for high performance in these areas.

  

2.      Oversee the school reporting structure and academic assessment plans and monitor their delivery.

  

3.      To advise the School Director on academic policy and carry overall responsibility for the school's academic life, including chairing the Academic Leadership Group and leading new initiatives such as curriculum reviews and effective academic monitoring of students.

  

4.      To act as line manager to the ALG, Academic Heads of Departments and University Advising departments.

  

5.      To oversee the Learning Support Department and monitor the provision of Learning Support.

  

6.      In conjunction with the Assistant Heads, monitor and analyse all school public examination results.

  

7.      Management of student data and trends regarding academic performance and potential, including but not limited to overseeing the analysis and dissemination of data from year group examinations (e.g. MIDYIS and ALIS) and overseeing target setting and the administration of other measures of value added and academic performance.

  



**LEADERSHIP OF STAFFING, INCLUDING RECRUITMENT**



1.      To be fully involved in recruiting new academic staff.

  

2.      To oversee the management of staff professional development days, inset and CPD (in conjunction with other members of the School Leadership Team).

  

3.      To be fully involved in new staff induction programmes (in conjunction with other members of the School Leadership Team).

  

4.      To work with the Director of Educational Systems to ensure the academic staff have regular and useful performance management reviews.

  

5.      Manage the school’s PGCE programme.

  



**LEADERSHIP OF WHOLE\-SCHOOL ACCREDITATION**



1.      To line\-manage the Accreditation Coordinator and ensure that all aspects of accreditation (CIS, NEASC, and IB) are well\-organised and well\-planned and that the School Director and School Council are fully informed about the progress of accreditation.

  



**MANAGEMENT OF UNIVERSITY ADVISING**



1.      management of the Director of University Advising.

  

2.      Ensure the School Director and other members of the School Council are fully informed regarding trends and patterns and new developments in university applications.

  

3.      Ensure the School Director and other members of the School Council are fully informed regarding Year 13 university offers.

  



**MANAGEMENT OF LEARNING SUPPORT AND EXAMINATIONS**



1.      management of the Head of Learning Support

  

2.      To work with the Head of Learning Support to oversee the applications for special consideration.

  

3.      To work with the Director of Educational Systems to ensure the planning and management of internal and external examinations

  

4.      To work with the Assistant Heads to ensure the accurate and timely analysis and publication of examination results

  



**MANAGEMENT OF SCHOOL EVENTS AND MARKETING MATERIALS**



1.      To work with other members of the School Council to ensure school events are well\-planned and run smoothly.

  

2.      To work with the Director of Educational Systems to ensure the well\-planning of Prize Giving, Graduation, and parent\-teacher events.

  

3.      To work with other members of the School Council to ensure the Aiglon Guide is updated annually.

  

4.      To work with the Marketing and Communications team and the Director of Educational Systems to ensure Aiglon Study Guides are accurate and available to the school community.

  



**DIVERSITY, EQUALITY AND INCLUSIVITY**



1.      Maintain up\-to\-date knowledge of the School’s DEIJ policies and procedures.

  



**SAFEGUARDING**



1.      Maintain up\-to\-date knowledge of safeguarding legislation and the School’s safeguarding policies and procedures and liaise closely with the Safeguarding lead.

  



**HEALTH AND SAFETY**



1.      Ensure that up\-to\-date knowledge of health and safety legislation applicable to the role is maintained and that the school’s health and safety policies and procedures are fully implemented and adhered to.

  



**PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT**



1.      Maintain and update personal knowledge and skills in line with legislation and the role's needs.

  



**GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES**



1.      To be actively involved in staff recruitment as required by the School Director.

  

2.      To be on hand out of hours in the event of an emergency.

  

3.      Attend school functions and events as often as possible and support students and staff in their activities and endeavours.

  

4.      To be a teacher in their specialist area with a reduced teaching load.

  

5.      To participate in the duty rota of School Council members on certain weekends and weekend evenings.

  

6.      To be a member of the Critical Incident team.

  

7.      To undertake any other reasonable tasks delegated by the School Director.

Early applications are encouraged. We reserve the right to appoint before the application deadline should we find the right candidate. Please apply through our School platform (eteach) following the instructions; applications sent by standard email will not be considered.



**Aiglon is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.**



**Applicants will therefore need to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post.**



You can find information on how the School processes your personal data within the School’s .



**JOB PURPOSE**



Aiglon College is an international boarding school based in the Swiss Alps with a worldwide reputation for providing a challenging holistic education in an inspiring setting within a safe, caring and supportive framework. The School is CIS accredited, and caters for around 500 students aged 7\-18 representing 70 nations. Students prepare for IGCSEs and the IB Diploma Programme.



Teachers are expected to make a significant contribution to the ethos of Aiglon College. The expectation is that staff will be positive and contribute enthusiastically to the life and work of the school. Teachers are directly responsible to the relevant Head of Faculty for the successful management of their classes and for the development and performance of students. The points listed in the job description below identify the key areas of this role; additional responsibilities may arise from time to time at the reasonable request of the School Director.



The ideal candidate for this position would be an experienced, enthusiastic, dynamic, knowledgeable leader and/or teacher of Physical Education and Sport. PE and Sport are compulsory for students throughout the and Senior schools. In Years 10 and 11 students have the option of studying IGCSE PE. Subsequently, in Years 12 and 13, Sports, Exercise and Health Science is offered and is currently taught in conjunction with the Science department.



KEY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
==============================



Professional Standards and Expectations
---------------------------------------



*      Carry out teaching duties and exercise responsibilities in line with the Guiding Principles of Aiglon;

  

*      Treat all members of the community, colleagues and students, with respect and consideration. Treat all students fairly, consistently and without prejudice;

  

*      Set a good example to students in terms of appropriate dress, standards of punctuality and attendance;

  

*      Read and adhere to the various policies of the school as expressed in the Aiglon Guide and other agreed documentation, and support the ethos of the school by upholding the behaviour code, uniform and kit regulations and other expectations;

  

*      Be available to work on campus in good time to complete all necessary preparations and meetings before the start of term;

  

*      Take personal responsibility for professional development and participate in staff training in line with the continued professional development programme of Aiglon;

  

*      Encourage members of their faculty to take responsibility for their own professional development and ensure all in the faculty participate in staff training in line with the CPD programme of Aiglon;

  

*      Reflect on personal and school practices in pursuit of continuous improvement.

  

*      Participate in appraisal and self\-evaluation activities and ensure the appraisal system is adhered to and completed within the faculty;

  

*      Chair a weekly faculty meeting;

  

*      Ensure all faculty members are aware of and adhere to departmental deadlines, policies and procedures;

  

*      Undertake pastoral and other duties, including weekend and evening duties, as prescribed within school policies;

  

*      Ensure that all deadlines are met as published in the school calendar and as directed by the Head of Faculty/Deputy School Directors;

  

*      Undertake professional duties that may be reasonably assigned, including cover and exam invigilation and ensure members of their faculty also undertake these duties;

  

*      Attend Assembly/Meditation on at least two mornings a week when averaged over any term and be prepared to give a Meditation once each year;

  

*      Be proactive and take responsibility for matters relating to health and safety;

  

*      Support the school through regular attendance at various events in the School Calendar (these may be religious, spiritual, sporting or cultural).

  



Departmental Management
-----------------------



*      Implement a clear vision for curriculum Physical Education and all aspects of Sport at Aiglon, making sure that there is continuity and progression between School and Senior School;

  

*      Develop and manage the strategic development plan for the faculty in line with the School’s strategic development plan thus fostering a love of Physical Education and inspiring a lifelong commitment to Sport;

  

*      management of Head of Physical Education and Sport, Head of Senior Physical Education and Sport, Head of Snowsports and Performance Athletes, MCFC football coach and the Sports Facilities Manager and support them in the management of all other members of the Physical Education and Sport faculty;

  

*      Ensure that the faculty embraces the opportunities available through strategic partnerships including MCFC;

  

*      Ensure the faculty handbook is updated annually and includes reference to objectives for the year ahead which tie into the school’s overall objectives;

  

*      Provide a strategic link between the Academic Leadership Group and the Physical Education and Sport faculty, attending meetings and reporting on School\-wide initiatives;

  

*      Ensure that the Department meets the curriculum requirements for the School;

  

*      Monitor and develop the quality of teaching, coaching and learning, through regular visits to lessons and otherwise, with a clear focus on excellence;

  

*      Implement a clear vision and structure for competitive inter\-school sport across the School at Aiglon;

  

*      Implement a clear programme for inter\-house sport at Aiglon. Liaise with the Director of Boarding and attend House Parent meetings where necessary to publicise and promote sporting initiatives, with clear communication to all stakeholders (students, staff and parents);

  

*      Promote and communicate to the Aiglon community initiatives and success stories from the Physical Education and Sport faculty, through weekly assemblies and the calendar alongside regular liaison with stakeholders in Admissions, Communications and Alumni teams;

  

*      Ensure that requirements of examination boards are met, and students are entered for public examinations, submitting appropriate coursework and ensuring that students are suitably prepared for examinations;

  

*      Preparing an annual report for the Deputy Director setting out an analysis of external examination results and value\-added statistics;

  

*      Ensure, in consultation with the Deputy School Director the effective deployment of staff and classes within the Department;

  

*      Participate in the appointment of new staff, and support new staff entering the Department;

  

*      Ensure all members of the faculty take account of students' prior levels of attainment, and baseline data where relevant, and use these to set targets for future improvements;

  

*      Oversee all aspects of the organisation of tournaments, fixtures and trips where appropriate;

  

*      To be available for School sporting events including The Challenge, Sports Day and other major School events;

  

*      Booking of snowsports instructors for all students in the winter term, which will require close liaison with external ski school instructors used by Aiglon, ensuring a high level of instruction takes place and to ensure ability groups are monitored regularly;

  

*      Prepare faculty budget requests for both operational and capital expenditure, within specified deadlines;

title: Data Privacy Specialist
description:
What you'll do
As a Data Privacy Specialist, you will join the Office of Data Privacy (ODP) in the Office of the CIO. ODP is CERN's independent and impartial centre of expertise in the area of data privacy. You will report to the Data Privacy Advisor, CERN's Data Protection Officer, and will advise CERN Management as well as Data Subjects and External Entities involved in the Processing of Personal Data, on all issues related to the Organization's data privacy protection.

Your responsibilities
-Provide specialised legal and operational advice to ensure that CERN's processing of personal data complies with applicable data privacy protection requirements throughout the data lifecycle, including projects, contracts, risk assessments, data transfers, and data breach response, taking into account data protection implications of emerging technologies.
-Manage or contribute to projects in the privacy and data protection field involving internal and external stakeholders (e.g. international data-sharing initiatives).
-Advise on the relevant governance structures, policies, documentation, stakeholder engagement, and establish and maintain regulatory relationships necessary to support CERN's data privacy protection framework.
-Ensure the effective exercise of data subject rights and the prompt handling of grievances and complaints.
-Promote a strong culture of data privacy protection through communication, awareness campaigns, guidance materials, and targeted training for CERN personnel and stakeholders.
-Oversee the effectiveness of CERN's data privacy protection framework, identify improvement opportunities, and ensure ongoing alignment with evolving regulatory expectations and recognised best practices.

Your profile
-You have proven data protection expertise and experience.
-You have extensive practical experience in data protection acquired at national or international level, in particular practical experience in applying data protection rules (preferably EU data protection framework).
-You preferably have experience working in an international environment and in dealing with EU actors and bodies or Inter-Governmental Organizations (IGOs).
-You will act with the required independence and impartiality.
-Master's degree or equivalent relevant experience in the field of Law, Data Protection, Privacy, IT or a related field. Holding a certification in the domain of data privacy protection (e.g. International Association of Privacy Professionals (IAPP), Certified Information Privacy Professional (CIPP)), or equivalent, or admission to the bar or equivalent legal qualification would be an asset.

Your skills
-Knowledge of EU regulations.
-Knowledge of administrative rules and procedures.
-Drafting and writing of official documents.
-Stakeholder relationship management, in particular data protection commissions, communities of DPOs of other IGOs.
-Risks assessment for compliance and data protection purposes.
-Compliance auditing.
-Delivers presentations in a structured and clear way; adjusts style and content to the audience; responds calmly and confidently to questions.
-Has a structured and organised approach towards work; is able to set priorities and plan tasks with results in mind.
-Is willing to work on different projects simultaneously.
-Maintains confidentiality.
-Spoken and written both English and French.

Be sure to meet the eligibility criteria
You are a national of a CERN Member State or Associate Member State. Currently, we cannot consider applications from Pakistani, Lithuanian, Latvian, Cypriot, Croatian and Turkish nationals, as the ceiling defined under Article II.5 of the Associate Membership Agreement has been reached.
You have relevant qualifications and professional experience.
If you have previously held a Staff contract at CERN, you will not be eligible for these positions.
Please pay attention to the additional criteria and requirements for this specific position and mentioned above.

Your CV (English or French)

Supervisor Bar (m/w/d)

Unternehmensbeschreibung

Unser Herz schlägt türkis.

Arbeiten bei Motel One ist wie zu Freunden kommen, wo Wertschätzung und Unterstützung großgeschrieben werden und die individuelle Persönlichkeit willkommen ist. Wir begegnen uns auf Augenhöhe und verstehen uns als ein Team: von der Geschäftsführung bis zu den Auszubildenden.

Mit unserer gemeinsamen Leidenschaft für modernes Design und hohe Servicequalität schaffen wir für unsere Gäste bei Motel One ein Zuhause für unterwegs. Unsere mehr als 95 Hotels in 13 Ländern überzeugen mit exklusivem Design, hohen Servicestandards und erstklassigen innerstädtischen Standorten zu einem attraktiven Preis.

Als Begründer und Vorreiter des Budget Design Konzepts expandieren wir erfolgreich in den Metropolen Europas und darüber hinaus. Werden Sie Teil unseres Teams und gestalten Sie gemeinsam mit uns Motel One.

Stellenbeschreibung

Gemeinsam mit deinen Gastgebertalenten bereicherst Du den Aufenthalt unserer Gäste. Neben der Koordination und Führung des Bar Teams, kümmest Du dich um:

- Betreuung und Beratung der Gäste in der Motel One Lounge sowie alle damit verbundenen Aufgaben
- Mitverantwortung für die Erreichung des Umsatzbudgets in der Motel One Lounge
- Sicherstellung eines reibungslosen und schnellen Serviceablaufs
- Mitverantwortung für die Durchführung von internen Coachings, Crosstrainings und Planung von Schulungen zur Weiterentwicklung der Barmitarbeitenden
- Bestellung von Lebensmitteln, Getränken und Spirituosen für die Bar sowie Durchführung von Inventuren zum Monatsende

Benefits:

- Bonus-Programm: Je besser die Gäste ihren Aufenthalt bewerten, desto höher fällt der Bonus für das ganze Team aus.
- International Karriere machen: Unsere nationalen und internationalen Hotels oder Neueröffnungen eröffnen zahlreiche Karrieremöglichkeiten.
- Günstig übernachten in ganz Europa: Vorteile sichern! Mit günstigen Personalraten in unseren Hotels in ganz Europa und in New York sowie weitere attraktiven Rabatten.
- Sich persönlich und fachlich weiterentwickeln: Mit einer umfangreichen Einarbeitung, jährlichen Schulungen und Coachings an der One University richtig durchstarten.
- Gemeinsam feiern: Ob Sommerfest, Weihnachtsfeier oder unser jährliches internationales Fußballturnier – Erfolge feiern wir gemeinsam mit dem Team.
- Kostengünstig und nachhaltig zur Arbeit: Es kann zwischen einem Zuschuss zum ÖPNV oder einem kostenlosen Fahrrad gewählt werden.

Qualifikationen

Ob als Hotelprofi oder im Quereinstieg – Du passt zu uns! Denn Persönlichkeit und Gastgeberqualitäten stehen bei uns an erster Stelle! Außerdem zeichnet dich aus:

- Ausbildung im Hotelfach bzw. Berufserfahrung in der Hotellerie/Gastronomie oder Interesse an einem Quereinstieg
- Freude an der Entwicklung von Mitarbeitenden – idealerweise erste Führungserfahrung
- Offenes, kommunikatives Auftreten sowie Gastgeberqualitäten und Leidenschaft für die Hotellerie
- Flexibilität und Kreativität sowie ein hohes Qualitätsbewusstsein auch in stressigen Situationen
- Teamfähigkeit und Bereitschaft abteilungsübergreifend zu unterstützen – Wir erreichen unsere Erfolge gemeinsam

Wir vergüten in Deutschland nach dem jeweils geltenden Tarifvertrag für das Hotel- und Gaststättengewerbe des jeweiligen Bundeslandes, in Österreich nach dem geltenden Kollektivvertrag für alle Arbeitnehmer:innen im Hotel- und Gastgewerbe und in der Schweiz nach dem L-GAV (Landes-Gesamtarbeitsvertrag des Gastgewerbes).

Bei Vollzeit gilt die für die Position angegebene Vergütungsspanne brutto/Monat, zzgl. variabler Vergütungsanteile und Benefits. Die konkrete Einstiegsvergütung innerhalb dieser Spanne richtet sich nach objektiven Kriterien, insbesondere nach Berufserfahrung und Qualifikation.
